A.explanation: Upward vertical force at P is wrong because the air-conditioning unit presses down on the beam at P.

B.explanation: Downward force at P with upward force at Q balances vertical forces, and the left-right pair balances horizontal forces with zero net moment.

C.explanation: Leftward force at P and rightward force at Q give a moment about Q in the same rotational sense as the downward load, so moments cannot balance.

D.explanation: Upward vertical force at P is wrong because it would lift the beam into the unit instead of supporting the downward weight.

hints: Notice the unit sits on the beam at P, so decide whether the contact force on the beam at P must act up or down.
For equilibrium the vector sum of horizontal forces must be zero and the vector sum of vertical forces must be zero, so the forces at P and Q must point in opposite senses.
Take moments about Q for the beam: the downward load at P is to the left of Q, so decide whether the horizontal force at P must point left or right to give an opposite moment.
walkthrough: Isolate the beam PQ. At the top end P it carries the weight of the overhanging air-conditioning unit, so the unit pushes down on the beam.
Therefore the vertical component on the beam at P must be downward. This leaves only the diagrams with down at the top end.
For force equilibrium, $\sum F_x = 0$ and $\sum F_y = 0$, so the vertical component at Q must be upward and the horizontal components at P and Q must be opposite.
Check moment equilibrium about Q. Let $x$ be the horizontal distance of P to the left of Q and $y$ the vertical height of P above Q.
A downward force $F_V$ at P gives moment $xF_V$ about Q, which must be cancelled by the horizontal force $F_H$ at P giving moment $yF_H$ in the opposite sense.
Only a horizontal force to the right at P, balanced by a horizontal force to the left at Q, gives $xF_V - yF_H = 0$ and can balance. A force to the left would add to the moment.
This combination of down and right at P with up and left at Q is option B.
